title: Accessibility Features 101 - Tools and Tips for Every Student
event: DCR x Writing Center Collaborative Workshop
blurb: Introducing students to free and open-source text to speech tools and built-in accessibility features on common software and platforms.

featured_slides.note: This slide defines accessibility broadly as 'adjustments to complete a task while minimizing strain,' framing it as a universal benefit rather than just a medical necessity. It sets a human-centered tone for the workshop by illustrating how small tweaks can help anyone working long hours.

Here, the presenter compares native accessibility settings on macOS and Windows, listing features like Live Captions and Zoom alongside their specific hardware limitations. This serves as a practical reference guide, encouraging students to explore the powerful tools already built into their operating systems before seeking third-party software.

The final content slide advises students to protect their time and attention, warning that managing complex file formats shouldn't feel like a full-time job. It reinforces the talk’s core philosophy that accessibility tools should streamline learning workflows, not add unnecessary friction or cognitive load.
